subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: goal too big for the time available [Revision]
passage: In Port Louis, Nour counted the coins in his biscuit tin for the third time: seventy rupees. The cycle in the shop cost two thousand. He did the sum with a stub of pencil. At ten rupees a week it would take nearly four years. "Four years?" By then he would be too tall for it. He put the pencil down. So he crossed out CYCLE on his chart and wrote FOOTBALL, three hundred. Then he walked to Uncle Yuki's stall. "Uncle, is there any work I can do on Saturdays? Washing crates?" Uncle Yuki looked at him for a moment. "Start this Saturday."

qa.q: How much did the cycle cost?
qa.a: The cycle cost two thousand rupees.

qa.q: What was Nour feeling when he saw the wait would be nearly four years?
qa.a: Disappointed but realistic, since he put the pencil down and picked a new goal.

qa.q: What other approach could Nour use for the cycle later, and why?
qa.a: He could look for a second-hand cycle or keep saving while earning on Saturdays, so the far goal comes closer.

qa.q: How might Uncle Yuki see Nour's request?
qa.a: Uncle Yuki probably sees a boy with initiative, which is why he says yes after a moment.

grounding: A boy sees that his target is too far away for his allowance, switches to a cheaper goal and asks about earning extra.

subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: goal too big for the time available [Revision]
passage: In Class 6 maths, Mrs Kulkarni wrote a problem on the board: "You save twenty rupees a week. How long to buy a cycle costing two thousand rupees?" Santosh worked it out quickly, and his face fell. A hundred weeks. Almost two years. That was his cycle, the red one in the shop near the bus depot. At break he sat on the school steps and redrew his plan: a cricket bat for six hundred first. Thirty weeks, still long but possible. Then another idea. After the last bell, his uncle, Darshan-mama, was waiting at the school gate as usual. "Mama, can I help with chores at your house on Sundays? Watering, sweeping the verandah? To earn a bit extra?" Darshan-mama smiled and said they would ask Santosh's mother together that evening.

qa.q: How many weeks would the cycle take at twenty rupees a week?
qa.a: A hundred weeks, almost two years.

qa.q: What did Santosh's falling face show?
qa.a: He felt disappointed and discouraged on realising the cycle was nearly two years away.

qa.q: What else could Santosh do if the chores bring in only a little?
qa.a: He could keep the bat as his first goal and talk with his family about whether the cycle might be a shared gift later on.

qa.q: How might Darshan-mama see Santosh's request?
qa.a: He seems pleased, smiling, and wants to ask Santosh's mother together, respecting both the effort and the family's say.

grounding: A boy sees his savings target is too far off, switches to a cheaper goal and asks his uncle about earning extra through chores.

subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: goal too big for the time available [Revision]
passage: I'm Imran, and Yusuf and I share a bench in class. For weeks he talked only about the geared cycle in the window of the cycle shop: two thousand rupees. Every Friday he counted his coins at lunch. Last Friday he stopped halfway, scribbled on the back of his notebook and went very quiet. I peeked: "25 a week... 80 weeks." Then he crossed out CYCLE and wrote "football boots, 500". After school I was with him when his Chacha came to pick him up. Yusuf asked straight out, "Chacha, can I wash your scooter on Sundays and help at the stall? For some extra money?" His Chacha laughed and said yes, starting this Sunday. Yusuf walked home faster than usual. I think he was happy. Or relieved.

qa.q: What did Yusuf write after crossing out CYCLE?
Why did Yusuf go very quiet last Friday?
qa.a: He had just worked out that the cycle would take eighty weeks, and he seemed discouraged before he changed his plan.

qa.q: Which approach would you suggest to Yusuf if the chores money stays small?
qa.a: Keep the boots as the next goal and look at the cycle again later, perhaps with his family, rather than dropping the idea altogether.

qa.q: How does Imran read Yusuf's mood on the way home?
qa.a: Imran sees Yusuf walking faster and guesses happy or relieved, without being sure which.

grounding: A classmate watches a boy realise his cycle goal would take too long, switch to boots and ask his uncle for chores.
